analysis.title: Public Service Enterprise Group (PEG): Focus on upcoming NJ filing to gauge regulatory environment improvement; Neutral
key_insights: GS stays Neutral on PEG after 3Q26 results. The stock is -8% YTD vs XLU +2%, and GS wants evidence of an improved New Jersey regulatory backdrop without overhang from ongoing studies of the utility business model.

PSE&G may file a proposal with the NJ BPU focused on regulatory lag on investments made since the last distribution rate case, instead of a traditional base rate case. Last quarter PSE&G said it planned a distribution base rate case by year-end 2026. The filing is meant to support the state's goal of keeping customer bills flat for as long as possible.
Management described discussions with the Sherrill administration as constructive. The filing timeline is unchanged at before year end.
The NJBPU Phase 2 business model review is moving forward. Options include multiyear rate plans, performance-based rates and earnings-sharing mechanisms.

PSE&G's annual transmission formula-rate filing is expected to raise annual transmission revenue by about $60mn from January 1, 2027, subject to true-up. NJBPU approved $14mn (IAP) and $8mn (CEF-EV) of annual revenue increases effective October 1.

FERC accepted parts of PJM's RBP proposal and rejected others. This pushes the RBP auction to March 2027 or later. The bilateral process for matching new generation with large loads remains open, and PEG is pursuing both paths.
Discussions with large-load customers on existing nuclear output, future nuclear uprates and other generation projects continue, with nothing to announce yet.
Management expects more opportunities in PJM's next transmission open window than in the last one, because congestion and pricing differences across the region are driving transmission needs.
GS sees these opportunities as potential upside to PEG's 6%-8% EPS CAGR through 2030. It wants signed contracts or project awards before adding meaningful upside to its estimates.

GS price target rises to $84 from $83 (SOTP-based, 12-month), implying an 18% total return. 2026-2028 EPS estimates are unchanged at $4.40/$4.71/$5.01. 2029/2030 EPS estimates rise to $5.32/$5.69 from $5.28/$5.67.

market_movers.rationale: Price target raised to $84 from $83 on the 3Q26 model update and a ~$60mn higher annual transmission revenue from 2027. GS stays Neutral pending detail on the NJ regulatory lag filing and signed contracts or project awards.

earnings_insights: PEG 3Q26 results reported (reported before 11/4/26). GS reflects reported earnings across PSE&G and Power & Other in its model.

GS 4Q26 estimate (GS estimate, not a print) includes the Salem 1 refueling outage and about $5.5mn of IAP and CEF-EV revenue roll-ins. The quarterly EPS table shows 9/26 at $1.15 and 12/26E at $0.85, 3/27E at $1.64, 6/27E at $0.85 (GS estimates).
Company growth target per the report: 6%-8% EPS CAGR through 2030.
risk_factors: A contract with a data center could accelerate earnings at Power (upside risk).
Regulatory shifts in New Jersey driven by customer bill affordability.
Potential upside to the current capital plan.
PJM remains uncertain, with the RBP auction pushed to March 2027 or later after FERC's partial rejection.
